characters.name: Dorothy Zbornak
characters.description: Allegedly Dateless: She seems to be going out on dates every other week, and has dated doctors, teachers, business owners, even an Admiral (also admittedly a few losers, but even then that's hardly 'dateless'). To listen to the other girls, however, you'd think she had never had a single date. Blanche and Sophia (and very rarely, Rose) make fun of her for it — though, ironically,Dorothyis the one who marries the former's uncle in the finale and leaves the latter to take care of Blanche and Rose, while Blanche and Sophia remain perpetually single, while Rose, the nicest to her, remains in a committed relationship with Miles but ends up breaking up with him inThe Golden Palace. Bookworm: A frequenter at the local library who always turns her books in on time... who are you to judge her? She's committed a great deal ofRaymond ChandlerandDashiell Hammettto memory...leading Sophia to quip, "you do this on first dates, don't you?" Brainy Brunette: As seen in flashbacks. Break the Haughty: Whenever she begins to think too highly of herself, Blanche, Sophia, or justlifesteps in to take her down. Butt-Monkey:Tends to have the worst luck when it comes to her personal life. Dorothy is actually a deconstruction of this trope, as the poor treatment she gets at the hands of her roommates (and has gotten all her life from her mother) is a large factor of why she keeps getting back together with Stan despite how badly it always goes.Frequently will ask an innocent question, only for it to turn into a series of insults. One time she found a strange rock under her bed. Marguerite, their housekeeper whom they suspected of practicing voodoo, put it there.Marguerite: I learned it from my grandmother. You put a specially-painted rock under a person's bed to guarantee a restful sleep. I figured with those bags under your eyes, you needed the rest.Rose: Dorothy always looks like that.Blanche: Besides, it'll take more than sleep to knock out those babies.Dorothy: Listen, why don't I just la

characters.name: Rose Nylund
characters.description: Berserk Button: Losing during sporting competitions, messing with her beloved teddy bear, and mocking her husband. Beware the Nice Ones: She can be a pretty big bitch if she wants. On the flip side, she can also be a force to be reckoned with if people are trying to exploit her or the girls. Tellingly, Dorothy, who once made a police officer break down in tears and "uprooted a mighty sequoia" when Rose lost her keys, is absolutely terrified ofeverpissing her off that badly. Brutal Honesty: Rose sometimes does this unintentionally, as her ditziness can prevent her from realizing when a situation requires tact. One time it was helped along byExhaustion-Induced Idiocy.Rose:Oh, Blanche. You're not a bad person. You're just horny all the time. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: She's a naive, childishCountry Mouse... who also happens to be a very effective grief counselor and mediator. One of her best moments in the series is her settling a decades long feud between Sophia and her daughter-in-law as both are grieving the loss of the former's son Phil, all in the span of five minutes. Even Dorothy couldn't pull that off. Rose is also shown to be a rather competent consumer advocate, holding onto the job for several years and advancing to the point she got her own assistant. She can also play the piano. Buxom Beauty Standard: Her ample bustline has been mentioned a couple of times, one time to psych Blanche out by pointing out that her shirt (a copy of Blanche's) only looks different on a busty woman.

characters.name: Blanche Devereaux
characters.description: A-Cup Angst: Despite being catnip on legs for most of the men of Miami, Blanche had a few episodes devoted to feeling a little inadequate in this regard. She considers implants in one episode, and in another, when Rose tries to psych her out at a bowling tournament by wearing the exact same outfit, Rose says not to worry because it looks different on a woman with a full bosom. In another episode, Blanche flirts with a man by claiming she is going to lie in a bath with "just enough water to barely cover my perky bosom", to which Sophia responds with "You're only gonna sit in an inch of water?" This is enough to set Blanche off.Blanche:Sophia, I've decided to wear this little watch on a chain nestled cunningly in my cleavage. What other accessories do I need?Sophia:Implants. Age Insecurity: She is so adamant about keeping her sex life alive that she had her age withheld by the governor. Alpha Bitch:Seems to have been one when she was a child if her stories are accurate. She grew up in a family of them. During Christmas one year, one of Blanche's sisters electrocuted her with the star of the Christmas tree, and then blamed her for the whole thing, which led their father to send her to her room and tell her that Baby Jesus was mad at her for ruining his birthday (and the electricity straightened her hair.) And let's not forgetVixen, Story of a Woman.Some of the stories of her exploits in high school also suggest this as well as mean girl tendencies. She once planned to marry the father of one of her cheerleading rivals, just so she could be the girl's "mama" and kick her off the squad. characters.name: Sophia Petrillo
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: "Pussycat" for Dorothy. She claims it's because she "loves pussycats and loves Dorothy" and because Dorothy was an excellent mouser at their Brooklyn apartment. It turns intoFamily Theme Namingwhen she calls Gloria "Kitten". Ailment-Induced Cruelty:Downplayedfor comedy. Sophia's a cantankerous (albeit often hilarious) old lady who says exactly what she thinks at all times. It's explained more than once that she had a stroke sometime prior to the series' beginning, and that it effectively destroyed her mental filter, so she can't help voicing whatever opinion pops into her head. Alter Kocker: Sophia wassupposedto be a Sicilian Catholic, but Estelle Getty, who was Jewish inReal Life, played her with many stereotypical Jewish New York traits. (In fact, Getty once went to the producers and asked them if they could just make Sophia Jewish, which would've made the character easier for her to play.) Her husband Salvatore was played the same way by Sid Melton, in a veryBorscht Beltcomedian style. This actually became aCasting Gagas the series went on — Sophia's Italian relations were mostly played by Jewish actors. Arranged Marriage: Hadtwo(or three; sometimes she speaks of her marriage to Dorothy's father as one). Ascended Extra: Was conceived as a recurringDrop-In Character, but audiences responded very positively to her, causing her to be added to the main cast.

characters.name: Stanley Zbornak
characters.description: Dorothy's ex-husband. He originally left Dorothy two years before the show began to marry a young flight attendant named Chrissy and live on Hawaii. However, he eventually moves to Miami and proceeds to be a lingering frustration in the lives of all the girls. Amicable Exes: How he wants to be with Dorothy. She, being the wronged party, is less willing to go for that if their kids aren't involved. By the finale, however, she accepts him as someone who will always be with her in some way, and they end the series as friends. Stan, to his credit, is more than happy with that arrangement.Dorothy:We weren't happy when we were married. We weren't happy when we were going to remarry. Maybe our relationship works best when we're just plain divorced. The Atoner: A big part of his characterization during the show is his repeated attempts to apologize to Dorothy for all the pain he put her through, only for Dorothy to repeatedly refuse. To be fair to Dorothy though, Stan would normally do or say SOMETHING off-putting that would remind Dorothy of why they didn't work out in the first place. Butt-Monkey: He's treated this way by all of the girls, even Rose. His ownmotherdidn't want him around. Casanova Wannabe: According to Dorothy, plus his obnoxious personality doesn't help.

characters.name: Angela Vecchio
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: Angela is implied to be the youngest of her siblings. Big Sister Instinct: Inverted in that Angela is actually younger than Sophia by two years, but she hits Tony with her purse for cheating on Sophia. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Angela is inexplicably never seen again despite her move to Miami setting her up as a recurringDrop-In Character.noteNancy Walker received a more regular role on a different show and didn't have enough time to reprise her role as Angela. Cool Aunt: To Dorothy. Aunt Angela and her mother are the two women Dorothy admired the most. Family Theme Naming: Angela has an older brother named Angelo who in turn was named after his father.

characters.name: Uncle Angelo
characters.description: Family Theme Naming: Angelo was named after his father. His sister, Angela, is named in the same vein, if slightly changed. Riches to Rags: At first he's a fairly successful business owner, but his business falls into financial foreclosure late in the series and he's forced to seek shelter in Miami, which leads to him living in the apartment Dorothy and Stan inherit and own. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: To his youngest sister Angela. After Angela couldn't fulfill her role as aDrop-In Characterrelated to Sophia for real-life reasons, their older brother Angelo was brought in to fill that role instead. Uncanny Family Resemblance: Bill Dana also played the siblings' father, Don Angelo, in a flashback.

characters.name: Salvadore Petrillo
characters.description: The Gambling Addict: Stated to be one, as Sophia tells Dorothy.Sophia: He was a gambler right up to his dying days. In fact, his last words were: "Ten bucks say I won't need this oxygen tank." Happily Married: To Sophia, while he was alive. Has a Type: Sal almost cheated on Sophia when she was pregnant with Phil. Sophia never met the would-be other woman but heard that she was a, "short, scrawny, bird-like thing who never shut up."Sophia:I guess variety is the spice of life. One-Steve Limit: Averted. Sophia mentions a SalvadoreDeMilowho attended a Christmas party with her and Sal Petrillo on December 24, 1955 and tried to kiss her. Posthumous Character: He's been dead for years before the series premier.

characters.name: Phil Petrillo
characters.description: The Ghost: Phil has been talked about by his sister Dorothy and mother Sophia but never shown. Even when he dies and the main cast attend his funeral, his body is never shown on screen. Happily Married: He and his wife, Angela, loved each other dearly and Angela fully supported Phil's cross-dressing. Wholesome Crossdresser: He liked to wear feminine clothing, and he was a good husband and father.

characters.name: Charlie Nylund Sr.
characters.description: Bigger Is Better in Bed: According to Rose, Charlie is so well-endowed that "a bull would have been jealous" upon seeing him naked. The Ghost: Unlike Blanche's and Sophia's late husbands, Charlie has never been shown. His best-known elements, based on Rose's accounts, are hiswell-endowed sex drive and, uh, "tool", as well as his imperfect history of employment and the resultant financial difficulties. The audience is only given a clue to his appearance onGolden Palace, when anIdentical Strangerstayed at the hotel. Happily Married: To Rose, until hisdeath. Identical Stranger: One showed up onGolden Palace(played by Eddie Albert). Money Dumb: According to Rose, could not balance a checkbook to save his life.

characters.name: Kirsten Adams née Nylund
characters.description: Broken Pedestal: All her life, she thought her father was a successful and hardworking businessman and was shocked to learn upon reading his will that he made very little money. Extremely Protective Child: When Rose undergoes triple bypass surgery, Dorothy, Blanche, and Sophia start singing to cope with their fears for Rose’s life. Kirsten mistakes this for callousness and forbids them from seeing her mother. She relents when Blanche declares they are going to mortgage the house to pay for mother’s therapy, and Dorothy tells Kirsten of their pact to always take care of each other. Funny Conception Story: Kirsten was conceived while her parents were dressed as sandwiches.

characters.name: Miles Webber
characters.description: Cutting Corners: Used as a plot device in "Ro$e Love$ Mile$", regarding his cost-cutting obsessions. The Scrooge: Miles was frugal to begin with, but he went overboard after a doctor told him he could live to be a hundred; he had only budgeted to live to eighty. Witness Protection: He turns out to have been under such a program, which forces him to flee, if briefly.

characters.name: George Devereaux
characters.description: Disappeared Dad: George's illegitimate son David never met him and didn't even learn of his paternity until after both parents had died. Happily Married: To Blanche, while he was alive, though that didn't stop him from having an affair that produced a child. Posthumous Character: He's already been dead for years prior to the series' start. Uncanny Family Resemblance:George Grizzardplayed both George and his younger brother Jamie.

characters.name: Skippy Devereaux
characters.description: The Ghost: Only ever mentioned onThe Golden Girls. We finally see him onThe Golden Palace.

characters.name: Melissa
characters.description: Babies Make Everything Better: Not between Janet and her husband but between Janet and her mother Blanche. They have a very rocky relationship to the point they stopped talking to each other. When Melissa was born, they tried to invoke this and patch their relationship. Unfortunately, it didn’t work. Cheerful Child: Melissa is a young girl who is happy to spend time with her grandmother. Unfortunately, she loses her cheerful disposition as Blanche pushes Melissa to compete in the Little Miss Miami Pageant. The Flapper: Blanche dresses her as one for the pageant. Pimped-Out Dress: Blanche makes Melissa try one on for the pageant.

characters.name: David
characters.description: One-Steve Limit: Averted, there are two Davids, and they're related to Blanche in different ways. One's her grandson, and the other's her accidental stepson.

characters.name: Clayton Hollingsworth
characters.description: All Gays Love Theater: Sophia claims that Clayton is the only man she's ever met who knows all the words to "Send in the Clowns". The Baby of the Bunch: Putting together the clues from Blanche's infamousVague Ageindicates that Clayton is the youngest of the five Hollingsworth siblings, as he is about twelve years younger than Blanche, which would logically put Virginia in between them. Funeral Banishment: He is notably absent at his father's funeral in Season 5. While this could usually be chalked up to the show's consistent use ofEstranged Soap Family, the fact that Clayton and Blanche are still on good terms in Season 6 creates the uncomfortable implication Clayton wasn't allowed to attendafter coming out the previous year.notebut since Virginia is the only person to speak to Blanche when she arrived it's ambigous if he's there or not. In the Blood: Blanche is greatly disturbed by the fact that she and Clayton have extremely similar taste in men. Late Coming Out: Clayton came out at the age of forty-five after beingmarried to a womanfor about twenty years.

characters.name: Virginia Hollingsworth
characters.description: Annoying Younger Sibling: To Blanche when they were younger. One story Blanche tells is the time Virginia almost electrocuted Blanche, and then immediately went crying to their father that Blanche was the one who electrocuted Virginia, for which Blanche was punished. The Glorious War of Sisterly Rivalry: Blanche and Virginia have never gotten along as children or as older adults. It took a near-death scare with kidney failure for Viriginia to do some soul-searching about how they've treated each other. Even without Blanche's involvement, Viriginia doesn't have a better relationship with their older sister Charmaine. Teen Pregnancy: Blanche implies that Virginia was shipped off as a teenager for being pregnant.Virginia:I was away at school!Blanche:Oh yes, the Good Samaritan Academy for the Knocked Up! "Two! Four! Six! Eight! All us girls are three months late!"
